items.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent –  Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
🪨 why use many token when few token do trick — Claude Code skill that cuts 65% of tokens by talking like caveman
items.reported_result: Maintainer reports an average 65% output-token reduction across ten prompts. Ponytail's separate agentic benchmark found Caveman used 7% more total tokens on twelve feature tasks despite producing less code.
items.main_caveat: It primarily changes model output, not reasoning or tool-input tokens. Lower response verbosity may have little or negative effect on total-session cost when deliberation and tool use dominate.

items.description: CLI proxy that reduces LLM token consumption by 60-90% on common dev commands. Single Rust binary, zero dependencies
items.reported_result: Maintainer reports roughly 60–90% reduction for supported command output. Tokbench independently observed 74.7% reduction on commands RTK touched, but those commands represented only about 2.5% of total spend in its N=1 pilot and the full run billed 27% more input tokens than native.
items.main_caveat: Operation-level compression does not guarantee lower task-level billing; command coverage, turn count, prompt caching, and harness design determine the addressable surface. The external result is a single-run pilot.

items.description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.reported_result: On twelve feature tasks with Haiku 4.5 and four runs per arm, the maintainer reports 54% fewer added lines, 22% fewer total tokens, 20% lower cost, and 27% less time, with 100% safety on a separate adversarial tier.
items.main_caveat: Results are model- and task-specific; gains concentrate in over-build traps and approach zero on irreducible work. The maintainer notes some reasoning models can spend more tokens under the discipline.

items.description: Pre-indexed code knowledge graph, auto syncs on code changes, for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, AntiGravity, Kiro, and Hermes Agent — fewer tokens, fewer tool calls, 100% local
items.reported_result: Across seven open-source codebases, the maintainer reports median results of 47% fewer total tokens, 58% fewer tool calls, 22% less time, and 16% lower cost, using four runs per arm.
items.main_caveat: The benchmark tests architecture questions rather than implementation tasks, is maintainer-run, and depends on graph accuracy and agent adoption of the MCP tools.

items.description: Compress tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. 60-95% fewer tokens, same answers. Library, proxy, MCP server.
Compress tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. 60-95% fewer tokens, same answers. Library, proxy, MCP server.
items.reported_result: Maintainer benchmarks report 47–92% savings on several agent workloads. Tokbench independently verified 342K tokens removed on wire in an N=1 pilot, but the run still billed 43% more input than native because it took more turns.
items.main_caveat: Verified per-request compression can be outweighed by longer execution paths. Compression fidelity, cache behavior, and total turns must be measured on the target workload; Tokbench replication was still pending.

items.description: 📦 Repomix is a powerful tool that packs your entire repository into a single, AI-friendly file. Perfect for when you need to feed your codebase to Large Language Models (LLMs) or other AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Gemini, Gemma, Llama, Grok, and more.
items.reported_result: No universal reduction percentage was reviewed; the --compress mode extracts key code elements to reduce token count.
items.main_caveat: Packing an entire repository can increase context use; aggressive filtering and compression are essential.

items.description: A powerful MCP toolkit for coding, providing semantic retrieval and editing capabilities  - the IDE for your agent
items.reported_result: README describes symbolic editing and retrieval as more token-efficient than full-file and search/replace workflows; no single token benchmark was reviewed.
items.main_caveat: Primary goal is semantic IDE capability, not token reduction alone; efficiency varies with language-server quality and tool usage.

items.description: Context window optimization for AI coding agents. Sandboxes tool output (98% reduction), persists session memory, and   enforces routing across 17 platforms via MCP + hooks.
items.reported_result: Maintainer examples report 315 KB reduced to 5.4 KB and 47 file reads totaling about 700 KB replaced by one 3.6 KB execution result.
items.main_caveat: The examples are not a neutral end-to-end benchmark. Generated analysis code and routing rules introduce correctness and sandbox boundaries; the repository uses Elastic License 2.0 rather than an OSI-approved license.

items.description: Replace 'hub' with 'ingest' in any GitHub URL to get a prompt-friendly extract of a codebase

items.description: Control what your AI can see. LeanCTX (Lean Context) is the context intelligence layer for AI agents — one local Rust binary that decides what they read, remembers what they learn, guards what they touch, and proves what they save. 60–90% fewer tokens as the receipt. 76 MCP tools, 30+ agents, local-first.
items.reported_result: Maintainer reports 60–90% fewer tokens for reads and shell output and cached rereads near 13 tokens. In Tokbench's N=1 external pilot, provider-billed input was 38% above native in MCP mode and 59% above native with the default integration.
items.main_caveat: The product covers many mechanisms, but end-to-end savings depend on whether agents actually use the optimized surfaces and whether additional tool calls increase total turns. The external benchmark is configuration-specific and single-run.

items.description: TokToken is a fast, single-binary C codebase indexer for AI coding agents. Powered by universal-ctags and SQLite FTS5, it provides precise symbol search, dependency tracking, and an MCP server. TokToken reduces LLM context token usage by 88-99% by retrieving exact code symbols instead of reading entire files. Zero runtime dependencies.
items.reported_result: Maintainer examples on Redis and Linux report roughly 88–99% fewer tokens for targeted symbol retrieval than full-file reads.
items.main_caveat: Depends on Universal Ctags plus custom parsers; static-call and import analysis can be incomplete in dynamic code.

items.description: The most intelligent context optimization engine for coding agents. Code-aware AST parsing across 17 languages. Command rewriting. Test, build, and git output compression. Token budget cascading. Built in Rust.
items.reported_result: Maintainer examples show code transformation modes ranging from light cleanup to roughly 90–95% reduction for signatures or types.
items.main_caveat: Aggressive structural modes deliberately omit implementations and are unsuitable when exact behavior is required.

items.description: Token-Reducing Shell — terminal output compression for AI coding agents
items.reported_result: Maintainer examples report 76% reduction for git status, 90% for cargo clippy, and 99% for an all-passing cargo test output; unsupported commands receive generic cleanup.
items.main_caveat: Examples are command-level reductions rather than an end-to-end coding-task benchmark, and parser coverage varies by command and platform.

items.description: Benchmark and plugin framework for measuring token-saving tools in agentic coding
items.reported_result: Pinned Cassandra tasks report 65.1–99.2% reductions for six tools, with exact validators and a second quality-retention layer.
items.main_caveat: Task-level artifact reduction is not the same as end-to-end session savings; workloads and agent behavior differ.

items.description: Independent eval of token-saving middleware (lean-ctx, rtk, headroom) on a real agentic SDLC workload — reproducible bench, raw transcripts, pre-registered protocol
items.reported_result: Its N=1 pilot found all tested middleware arms billed more input tokens than native on a context-frugal harness, even though Headroom verifiably removed 342K tokens on wire; multi-run replication was pending.
items.main_caveat: The harness author discloses product conflicts, the pilot uses one task and provider, and single-run total differences cannot establish general performance; its main value is methodology and counter-evidence.

items.description: Same answer, fewer tokens — KO-first LLM output-compression skill for Claude Code & Codex. A Korean-native caveman alternative, measured on real session output_tokens.
items.reported_result: Maintainer reports paired-median output reductions near 70% for Korean and 73% for English on Claude Opus 4.8, with held-out cross-checks near 71% and 68%.
items.main_caveat: The main evaluation uses one run per prompt and replaces the normal Claude Code system prompt to isolate register effects; real sessions may differ and only output tokens are measured.

items.description: LLM context compression proxy — 40-70% token savings, zero code changes
items.reported_result: Maintainer reports 40–70% token-bill reduction, with BFCL and other dataset scripts included for compression and quality checks.
items.main_caveat: Compression can alter tool schemas or code semantics; per-transform quality should be tested on the target workflow.

items.description: Say more with less. Claude Code skill/plugin that cuts ~60-70% of output tokens while keeping natural, readable English.
items.reported_result: Maintainer claims roughly 60–70% fewer output tokens and provides before-and-after examples, but no reviewed task-level benchmark was found.
items.main_caveat: The claim is output-only and example-based; it does not measure reasoning, tool calls, total session tokens, or answer-quality regressions.

items.description: Three lean tools for Claude Code: a YAGNI code discipline, a config-drift auditor (/whippet-config), and a code↔docs drift hook.
items.reported_result: In a 13-task Opus 4.8 screen, the maintainer reports little code-size or dependency reduction versus baseline, but more persistent runnable checks and additional trust-boundary validation.
items.main_caveat: The evaluation is small, one run per cell, and does not demonstrate token savings on the tested strong model; its value is primarily workflow discipline rather than proven cost reduction.

items.description: Why waste time say lot word when few word do trick? Claude Code skill that cuts ~35-45% output tokens.
items.reported_result: Maintainer projects 35–45% lower net output, including 60–70% less prose and no reduction in code tokens.
items.main_caveat: The figures are projections rather than a published measured benchmark, and the skill does not address input, reasoning, or tool-output tokens.

items.description: Output compression for AI coding agents
items.reported_result: README claims about 75% fewer output tokens and ships a live-model benchmark harness, but no completed aggregate benchmark results were reviewed.
